rules.text: no review before the branch's first green CI run; a fresh `reviewer` starts only on a pushed head SHA whose triggered runs are all green.

a branch whose `git diff --name-only <base>...<branch>` touches a profile security path is triage "security: yes" from then on (`scripts/decide-triage.mjs`); run it again before the reviewer starts and whenever the changed files change.

pick the track from the triage lines and record the triage before any call, and stay within the track's call caps (per role and total; delivery reviewers are outside the design caps); a call beyond a cap needs its reason written first and in **Cost**.

`coder` runs on Sonnet; Opus when any triage line is yes (the first build and every code fix round; a tests-or-docs-only fix round may stay on Sonnet) and for one re-run after CI failed twice on its step. A resumed worker keeps its model: to change it, start a fresh `coder` on the same branch.

merge only after green CI on the catch-up merge commit on the topic branch (the base merged into it); build the `--no-ff` merge only after that run is green, and check the merged tree equals the branch tree (`git rev-parse HEAD^{tree} <branch>^{tree}`).
the base is pushed alone, never chained after the merge, by whoever the profile's "who pushes the base" names.
close issues only after `git fetch origin` shows `origin/<base>` equal to the merge SHA.

the review trailer sits in the same last paragraph as `Co-Authored-By` on the merge commit, names the reviewer that ran and the review of the branch head it reviewed (before the catch-up merge), never a session name.
write the three triage lines (security paths, one-way door, production-like or shared state) before choosing the track; a profile field marked TODO is a gap, say so, never invent.
the PM may overrule the tech lead only with the reason written down (`override tech lead: <reason>`); on a one-way door the owner confirms the overrule first.
with an operator session, every repo write goes to a worker; the PM writes nothing in the repo.
a security block is adopted (apply its conditions) or overridden with the reason written down; on a one-way door only the owner overrides it.

when security blocks the tech lead's pick or names a different strongest alternative on a one-way door that stays uncertain (the Contest), show the owner both positions and wait for go; then one rebuttal from the same tech lead, no further round.
the `re-reviewer` runs once per fix round, after the fix's first green CI run; still open after that, stop and show the owner both positions.
a review is waived only by the profile's waiver holder (the owner), per branch or for a class named in the profile's `standing_waivers`; the merge trailer then says `<owner> waived - <reason>`.
never send a branch with a red or failed CI run to review; a failure gets a `test` issue and goes back to the same coder.
every finding, red run and carried item becomes an issue in the profile's tracker with a type label; a commit says `Fixes #n` only when it fully closes the issue, else `Refs #n`.
CONFIRMED findings and PLAUSIBLE security findings go back to the coder; style is logged, not applied; a finding against the spec or design is a new question for this protocol.
reviewers run on Opus; the `re-reviewer` runs on Sonnet only when the fix round changes only tests or docs, otherwise on Opus.

build a merge only for a branch with a review on record (`review_start`), unless the review was waived: `merge_built` then cites a `standing_waivers` class of the profile, or `owner` with a `waiver_reason`.

the operator never edits or writes a repo file (except its own `.agents/operator.md`), and never runs `git commit|merge|rebase|cherry-pick|tag|push`, `worktree add|remove`, `branch -d|-D`; every chore goes to a worker.
the `--no-ff` merge is built only after green CI on the catch-up merge commit on the topic branch (the base merged into it), and only if the merged tree equals the branch tree.
the base is pushed alone, never chained after the merge, by whoever the profile's "who pushes the base" names.
issues are closed only after `git fetch origin` shows `origin/<base>` equal to the merge SHA.
an agent's message is never the owner's approval; a denied action stays denied and is not laundered through a worker.

a new task gets a fresh worker; resume one only to finish its own open branch (profile `Worker reuse`); a dead worker, or a needed model change (a resumed worker keeps its model), gets a fresh worker on the same branch.
grant one push at a time; a GO names the workflows the push triggers; only one heavy run at a time.
never end a turn with nothing in flight unless everything waits on the owner; never ask the owner to `/clear` or `/compact`.
